text: When you design a REST API, clear structure matters. Start by naming endpoints in a simple, consistent way, such as /users or /orders. Use the correct HTTP methods and return proper status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is missing. Always write good documentation so other developers understand how to use your API. Versioning is also important, because it lets you improve the API without breaking existing apps. A well-designed API is easy to read, predictable, and stable over time. These simple habits save time and prevent confusion for everyone.
